scenarios.label: Prerender + Per-Crawler
scenarios.blurb: Headless render → HTML for search crawlers, Markdown for AI crawlers, per-crawler from one cached render. Powers the "Who's asking?" view.

scenarios.label: Convert + Cache
scenarios.blurb: Harper self-populates Markdown from the prerendered HTML; Akamai Functions is the fallback converter.

scenarios.label: Write-through MD Cache
scenarios.blurb: First AI crawler converts via Akamai Functions and writes through to Harper; returning bots are served from Harper cache.
scenarios.blockedReason: Needs the DNS cutover — the edge converter can't reach the real origin until stopwaitingshipit.com points at Akamai.

scenarios.label: Edge Convert + CDN Cache
scenarios.blurb: Akamai Functions converts HTML→Markdown at the edge; the CDN caches the result; no Harper.
scenarios.blockedReason: Needs the DNS cutover — the edge converter can't reach the real origin until stopwaitingshipit.com points at Akamai.

_notes.collapsed: All scenarios target ONE property (stopwaitingshipit.com) — the commerce clean-room deployment. The unified EdgeWorker selects the scenario per request from the X-Demo-Scenario header (= ewScenario), enabled by PMUSER_DEMO_MODE=true. One EW, one property. The 'Who's asking?' hero uses the prerender scenario and varies only the crawler.
_notes.status: prerender + convert-cache verified live through the staging edge (harper-cache-html / harper-cache-md). md-cache + cdn-cache are blocked on DNS cutover (the edge converter can't reach the real origin until stopwaitingshipit.com DNS points at Akamai).
_notes.ewScenario: Sent as the X-Demo-Scenario header; maps to the EdgeWorker's demo-mode preset (cdn-cache | md-cache | convert-cache | prerender).
_notes.run: Staging demo: AKAMAI_STAGING=1 HARPER_PREVIEW_URL=<harper-cluster-url> HARPER_BOT_KEY=eeo-commerce-demo npm start
